title: World roundup: Houthi-Saudi fighting spreads to ports, Ukraine strike in Libya kills 2, Cairo tanker fire kills 31
key_points: Houthi rebels and the Saudi-led coalition traded strikes on ports and oil sites; Iran says 2 more tankers hit mines.
Two Libyan officers died after a Ukrainian drone attack on a Russian warship in Benghazi.
Drone strikes in Sudan's Blue Nile state killed about 19 civilians, rights groups say.
A fuel tanker fire on a Cairo highway killed at least 31 people; the US proposed new tariffs on 14 economies.
content:
Here are the biggest world stories of the last 24 hours, and what they mean for Kenyans and Africans.

1. Houthi-Saudi fighting spreads to ports and oil sites

Fighting between Yemen's Houthi rebels and the Saudi-led coalition grew this week. On Tuesday a Houthi drone hit a tower in Riyadh's financial district. Saudi authorities said 11 people were hurt. The coalition then struck Hodeidah port in Yemen, which, according to the UN, handles most of Yemen's aid. No casualty figures were given.

On Wednesday the Houthis said they hit Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura oil refinery. The coalition said it shot down four drones there and did not confirm any hit. The Houthis also told workers at Saudi Red Sea ports, including Jeddah, to leave. Early Thursday the coalition said it stopped two missiles aimed at Riyadh, Anadolu reported.

Separately, Iran's Revolutionary Guard said two more oil tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday. The ships were not named and the claim has not been independently confirmed.

Why it matters: Many Kenyans live and work in Saudi Arabia and the Gulf. Higher oil prices also push up fuel costs at home.

2. Ukraine's war reaches Libya

Two officers of Khalifa Haftar's Libyan National Army died on Tuesday of wounds from a Ukrainian sea-drone attack on a Russian warship in Benghazi on Sunday, AP and Al Jazeera reported. Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed the attack. Kyiv says the ship was sunk; Libyan officials told AP it was badly damaged. The Libyan army has vowed to respond. Ukraine said it did not target Libyans.

Why it matters: Analysts say the attack could disrupt Russia's supply route to its forces in the Sahel, pulling Africa deeper into a war far away.

3. Sudan: drone strikes kill civilians in Blue Nile

Night drone strikes on homes in Damazin, capital of Sudan's Blue Nile state, killed 19 civilians on Tuesday, according to the rights group Emergency Lawyers. The Sudan Doctors Network gave a toll of 17. Both groups blamed the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF), which did not respond to Reuters. Blue Nile borders South Sudan and Ethiopia.

Why it matters: Fighting near East Africa's borders raises the risk of more people fleeing to neighbouring countries.

4. Egypt: tanker fire on Cairo highway kills 31

A fuel tanker crashed and caught fire on the Ring Road in Giza, part of Greater Cairo, on Wednesday evening. Egypt's Health Ministry said at least 31 people died and 21 were injured. More than two dozen vehicles burned. The cause has not been confirmed.

5. US proposes new tariffs on 14 economies

The US Trade Representative proposed new import taxes on 14 trading partners, including China, the European Union, India and Vietnam. Trade chief Jamieson Greer said most rates would be 15 to 20 percent and nothing would start for at least a couple of months, according to reports quoting CNBC. Public hearings start in January. No African country is on the list. Asian stock markets fell on the news.

Why it matters: Some of Kenya's competitors in selling clothes to the US are on the list, while Kenya is not.
